steps.tx: **Extrapulmonary tuberculosis** is Mycobacterium tuberculosis disease outside the lungs, forming 15 to 20% of tuberculosis in HIV negative and fifty percent in HIV positive patients. Lymph node disease makes 30% of extrapulmonary cases, while meningeal disease carries fifty percent mortality without therapy. India reports about five hundred thousand extrapulmonary cases yearly, with children having higher lymphatic spread. Culture confirms only fifty percent of lymph node cases, so tissue diagnosis often exceeds microbiology.
steps.say: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis is disease outside the lungs. It forms fifteen to twenty percent of tuberculosis in hiv negative patients and half in hiv positive patients. Lymph node disease is the commonest form. Culture confirms only half the cases.

steps.tx: **Risk factors** include HIV with CD4 below 200, diabetes, high dose steroids above 15 milligrams for over 4 weeks, and tumour necrosis factor blockers. Young children below 5 years develop disseminated disease in twenty five percent after primary infection. About 15% of immunocompetent patients develop extrapulmonary disease from silent haematogenous spread years later. Prior bacille Calmette Guerin vaccination does not protect against nodal disease in adults.
steps.say: Risk factors include hiv with low cd four counts, diabetes, prolonged steroids and biologic drugs. Young children develop widespread disease often after primary infection. About fifteen percent of healthy patients develop extrapulmonary disease years later. Vaccination does not protect adults against nodal disease.

steps.tx: **Spread** occurs by lymphatic, haematogenous, and contiguous routes. Cervical nodes drain the tonsil and cause scrofula with matted nodes, cold abscess, and sinus discharge in 40%. Genitourinary disease shows sterile pyuria with flank pain and calcified kidney in computed tomography. Bone disease starts in metaphysis and collapses vertebrae, producing a gibbus and psoas abscess. Peritoneal disease imitates ovarian cancer with ascites and raised cancer marker CA one two five.
steps.say: Spread occurs by lymphatic, blood and contiguous routes. Neck nodes drain the tonsil and may discharge through skin in forty percent. Urinary disease presents with sterile pyuria and flank pain. Bone disease collapses vertebrae and makes a hump. Peritoneal disease imitates cancer with fluid in the abdomen and raised markers.

steps.tx: **Clinical features** are localised and prolonged. Lymph node tuberculosis gives painless swelling above 2 centimetres with matting and fluctuation, fever in 60%, and weight loss. Tuberculous meningitis shows headache, cranial nerve palsies, and hydrocephalus in fifty percent, with rapid decline over 2 weeks. Enteric disease causes ileocaecal mass with obstruction mimicking Crohn disease. Genital tuberculosis causes infertility in fifty percent of endometrial cases. Night sweats are less prominent than in lung disease.
steps.say: Lymph node tuberculosis gives painless enlarging nodes with matting and fever. Meningitis presents with headache, nerve palsies and hydrocephalus with rapid decline. Gut disease causes mass with obstruction. Genital disease causes infertility in half the endometrial cases. Night sweats are less prominent than in lung disease.

steps.tx: **Nontuberculous mycobacteria** disease differs in host and site. Mycobacterium avium complex infects CD4 below fifty with disseminated disease in 70%, while Mycobacterium kansasii causes cavitary lung disease imitating tuberculosis. Mycobacterium marinum follows fish tank injuries with sporotrichoid spread in fifty percent. Mycobacterium fortuitum follows surgical wounds and dialysis. Treatment needs 12 months of macrolide based therapy, not the 4 drug tuberculosis regimen quoted at the bedside.
steps.say: Nontuberculous mycobacteria differ in host and site here. Avium complex affects low cd four counts with widespread disease. Kansasii causes cavitary lung disease imitating tuberculosis here. Marinum follows fish tank injuries with spreading nodules today. Fortuitum follows surgical wounds in many patients recently. Treatment needs long macrolide based therapy here.

steps.tx: **First test** for nodal disease is fine needle aspiration showing caseous necrosis with epithelioid granulomas in eighty percent, plus cartridge based nucleic acid amplification with 85% sensitivity. The gold standard is culture of pus or tissue on liquid media with drug susceptibility in 2 to 4 weeks. Cerebrospinal fluid shows lymphocytic pleocytosis with low sugar and high protein exceeding one hundred milligrams per decilitre. Ultrasound shows matted nodes with intranodal calcification in chronic disease.
steps.say: Do fine needle aspiration for granulomas and rapid molecular test. The gold standard is culture with susceptibility testing. Spinal fluid presents high protein with low sugar. Ultrasound presents matted nodes with calcification in chronic disease.

steps.tx: **Molecular and imaging** tests fasten diagnosis. GeneXpert detects rifampicin resistance in 90% of smear positive nodal pus, while line probe assays detect isoniazid resistance. Magnetic resonance shows meningeal enhancement with infarcts in tuberculous meningitis, while spine imaging shows disc destruction with paravertebral abscess. Potassium hydroxide mount is negative in tuberculosis, separating it from fungal disease. A composite score combining cytology, molecular test, and culture outperforms any single test.
steps.say: Molecular tests fasten diagnosis. Rapid cartridge tests detect rifampicin resistance in most cases. Brain scan presents membrane enhancement with infarcts in meningitis. Spine imaging presents disc destruction with abscess. A combined score of cytology, molecular test and culture outperforms any single test.

steps.tx: **First line management** for most extrapulmonary disease is 2 months of rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol followed by 4 months of rifampicin and isoniazid. Ethambutol 20 milligrams per kilogram daily and isoniazid three hundred milligrams daily with vitamin cover prevent optic and nerve toxicity. Rifampicin six hundred milligrams daily remains the backbone. Bedaquiline four hundred milligrams daily for 2 weeks then 200 milligrams thrice weekly is reserved for drug resistant forms.
steps.say: Treatment is two months of four drugs followed by four months of two drugs. Ethambutol and isoniazid doses are by weight. Rifampicin remains the backbone. Newer drugs are reserved for drug resistant forms.

steps.tx: **Site specific** therapy adds measures. Meningeal tuberculosis needs 12 months total with steroid cover at zero point four milligrams per kilogram daily for 6 weeks. Genitourinary disease needs 6 months with urology repair for strictures after 5 months. Spinal tuberculosis needs 9 to 12 months with bracing and early surgeon review if cord compression threatens. Lymph node abscess needs aspiration, not incision, as surgery spreads sinuses. Pleural tuberculosis needs steroids only with constrictive physiology, not routine use.
steps.say: Site specific therapy starts with measures for each site. Meningeal disease needs twelve months with steroids here. Urinary disease needs six months with repair later on. Spine disease needs longer therapy with bracing here. Needle aspiration serves abscess of the node here. Surgery spreads the disease so avoid cutting often.

steps.tx: **Complications and prognosis** include hydrocephalus in fifty percent of meningeal cases, spine collapse with paraplegia in 10% of Pott disease, and constrictive pericarditis in 30% of pericardial disease. With complete therapy, cure exceeds 90% for nodal disease but meningeal mortality stays 20 to 30%. Drug resistant nodal disease has below 60% success without bedaquiline. Follow up ultrasound at 6 months confirms node shrinkage and guides stoppage.
steps.say: Complications are hydrocephalus in half of meningeal cases, spine collapse and constrictive pericarditis. Cure is above ninety percent for nodal disease but meningeal mortality stays high. Drug resistant disease results less often without newer drugs. Follow up scans confirm shrinkage and guide stopping.

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam** locks sites, fluids, and regimens in one frame. Meningeal fluid shows lymphocytic pleocytosis with high protein, spine disease spares disc posteriorly early, and genital disease causes infertility. Avium complex needs targeted prophylaxis below fifty CD4 counts. Miliary pattern on chest X-ray suggests haematogenous spread. Stereotyped numbers such as 6, 9, and 12 months are the regimen answers examiners expect.
steps.say: Keep sites, fluids and regimens together in one frame. Meningeal fluid presents high protein with low sugar. Avium complex needs prophylaxis at very low cd four counts. Miliary shadowing on x ray suggests blood spread. Six, nine and twelve months are the regimen answers examiners expect.
